answer: Ephemeral Reputation Decay Ledger. Each new identity starts at zero visible score, and any positive action must spiral through a public ledger whose entries decay on a fixed half-life. Clones can harbor no transferable history, so a fresh identity earns nothing from its parent's record. To reach useful standing, an attacker must operate every clone through enough genuine transactions to survive decay, paying full compute and coordination costs per identity while the ledger stays hollow of shortcuts. Marginal clone EV goes negative because registration and upkeep exceed expected value.
